claim: Claude API output tokens cost approximately 5x the price of input tokens across all model tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable), making uncapped response length a primary driver of unexpected cost.
quoted_support: Output tokens cost five times as much as input tokens across all model tiers, which means uncapped response length is one of the fastest ways for a production bill to exceed projections.

claim: Prompt caching reduces Claude API input costs by up to 90% on cache hits, and placing static content first in the prompt (before dynamic content) is required to maintain a stable cache boundary.
stance_target: cost optimization techniques for agentic loops (Pillar 6)
scope_conditions: Anthropic Claude API prompt caching mechanics, 2026
quoted_support: A cache hit costs only 10% of the standard input price... Placing static content first in the prompt creates a stable cache boundary, with dynamic content following. Teams that let system prompts vary or insert dynamic fields early break the cache on every request and pay full price each time.

claim: Anthropic's Batch API gives a flat 50% discount on both input and output tokens across all model tiers for workloads tolerating up to 24 hours of processing latency.
quoted_support: The Batch API offers a flat 50% discount on both input and output tokens across all model tiers for workloads that tolerate up to 24 hours of processing time.

claim: Agentic and multi-turn workflows account for over 50% of enterprise Claude API token consumption, and because each turn resends the full conversation history, costs compound sharply over long sessions (a 14-token question can cost over $2 by the 260th exchange).
stance_target: cost risk of long-running agentic loops / continuous operation (Pillar 5/6)
quoted_support: Agentic and multi-turn workflows account for over 50% of enterprise API token consumption, according to the Anthropic Economic Index September 2025 Report... every new request in a multi-turn conversation resends the full conversation history, so a 14-token question that costs fractions of a cent at the start of a session can cost over two dollars by the 260th exchange.
numbers: 40-60% cost reduction by truncating to last 5-10 turns

claim: A company's Claude API spend reportedly grew from $500,000/month to $10 million as usage volume scaled while routing logic remained flat, illustrating unconstrained cost blowup from single-model-for-everything architecture.
stance_target: necessity of complexity-based model routing for cost control (Pillar 6)
scope_conditions: single unnamed company, cited via vendor LinkedIn post, unverified by primary filing
quoted_support: Companies spending $500k on Claude API bills in December are now spending $10M... When volume grows but routing logic stays flat, the cost curve bends sharply upward.

claim: Sonnet 5 and later Claude models use a newer tokenizer that generates roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier model versions, silently increasing per-request cost.
stance_target: hidden cost drivers in model migration (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: Sonnet 5 and later models use a newer tokenizer that generates roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier versions.
